discovery: Optical lattice atomic clocks reaching 10^-18 precision and accuracy

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision metrology
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock in 2001: neutral atoms are trapped in an optical lattice tuned to a 'magic wavelength', so the trap shifts the upper and lower clock states equally and the atoms can be probed without Doppler or recoil effects. This combines the quantum-projection-noise advantage of many atoms with the isolation of a single trapped ion. Ye turned the concept into a metrology platform. He used femtosecond frequency combs and ultrastable lasers to reach systematic uncertainties and instabilities near 10^-18. He also resolved many-body interactions among the clock atoms and measured gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample. Lattice clocks have improved timekeeping by more than two orders of magnitude, and they now drive the planned redefinition of the SI second, relativistic geodesy, and searches for dark matter and for variation of the fundamental constants. Their impact across physics is broad and rigorously quantified.
